minutes.headline: Sewer Commission thanked retiring member Carl and backed adding jetting and SSO response to the MP operations contract.
minutes.summary: The commission honored Carl on his resignation after 15 years, then discussed the Fitchburg sewer use ordinance changes, new MP control panels, and the year-two operations contract with SSO response and jetting coordination added. The business manager reported on counsel's opinion, invoices and website updates. April 13 minutes were approved and the meeting adjourned. A later start time of 5:30 was discussed but not formally decided.

votes.outcome: passed (ayes heard from Mike, John, Brett and the chair)

budget_items.what_was_said: Town meeting approved all sewer articles, including a part-time position.
The first-year contract ran nine months; it renews for two more years with edits adding SSO response and jetting coordination. Pricing could change and might require going out again.
The April counsel invoice covers review of bylaws and an opinion, and is processed through town hall.
Fitchburg usage charge through the end of April was reported; budgets are said to be doing well.
The current charge for a reconnection permit was raised for future review.

Staff to send a written response to a resident's question about the 330 gallons per day, copied to town counsel and town officials.
Next meeting set for May 25 at five o'clock, with the following meeting June 8, probably 5:30, and a reorganization of the board.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission recorded no votes on the MP operations contract, but discussed adding jetting coordination and SSO response to it, pending MP's agreement and counsel review.
The contract's first year ran nine months and renews for two more years; pricing could change and might require going out to bid again.
The commission honored a retiring member on his resignation after 15 years.
The business manager is to ask the town manager whether town counsel may attend a future meeting, and staff are to answer a resident's question in writing.
April 13 minutes were approved; the next meeting is set for May 25, with a June 8 meeting and a board reorganization to follow.

why_it_matters: The operations contract covers the town's sewer system, and adding overflow response and jetting could change what the town pays MP, so sewer rate payers may see a price change if the contract is repriced.
A June reorganization of the board will decide who sits on the commission that sets those contract terms.
